Cuthah
KYOO-thuh
proper noun / place
From Hebrew Kuthah / Kuth, a Mesopotamian city; source of colonists in Samaria who made Nergal their god.

📖 Biblical Definition

Cuthah is the city from which the king of Assyria brought men to dwell in Samaria after Israel was carried away. The record lists Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim as the seedbeds of the new population. Then the text adds that the men of Cuth made Nergal. Cuthah therefore stands beside Sepharvaim as a named source of post-exilic idolatry on holy soil. The empire’s resettlement policy did not create a blank religious field; it imported shrines. The people feared the LORD after a fashion because lions slew some of them, yet they continued the service of their own gods. Cuthah’s Nergal is one line in that indictment. The place-name teaches that judgment-emptying without true conversion leaves a vacuum that superstition fills. Samaria’s later mixture religion had addresses of origin, and Cuthah was one of them. The church should hear the warning whenever a land once taught the law becomes a depot for foreign gods under the thin cover of civil order or cultural exchange. The LORD will not share His name with Nergal, whether the altar is ancient bronze or modern branded spirituality dressed in borrowed sacred words.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Mesopotamian city that supplied colonists for Samaria; the men of Cuth made Nergal their god.

expand to see more

CUTHAH, also Cuth, a Mesopotamian source of Samaria’s settlers.

Assyria planted men from Cuthah in Israel’s emptied cities.

The men of Cuth made Nergal their god.

Their religion mixed with a form of the fear of the LORD.

Cuthah names one root of Samaria’s syncretism.

📖 Key Scripture

2Ki 17:24 — "And the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel: and they possessed Samaria, and dwelt in the cities thereof."

2Ki 17:30 — "And the men of Babylon made Succothbenoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima,"

2Ki 17:33 — "They feared the LORD, and served their own gods, after the manner of the nations whom they carried away from thence."

2Ki 17:34 — "Unto this day they do after the former manners: they fear not the LORD, neither do they after their statutes, or after their ordinances, or after the law and commandment which the LORD commanded the children of Jacob, whom he named Israel;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Cuthah is not a neutral migration note; it is a ledger entry of imported idolatry after covenant judgment.

expand to see more

The corruption is to celebrate religious diversity in Samaria as early pluralism. Scripture calls it sin. Cuthah’s Nergal is not a heritage festival. It is a rival god on soil that had heard the law. Modern churches that collect spiritualities like souvenirs are walking the Cuthah road. The remedy is the exclusive worship of the LORD, not a negotiated pantheon with biblical vocabulary.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. What must be recovered is the conviction that biblical geography is not scenery for myth, but the real theatre of the LORD’s providence, judgment, and grace. The places of Scripture stand as witnesses that God acts in history, among real peoples, on real soil, for the glory of His name.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Cuthah is the Mesopotamian origin of settlers who brought Nergal into the cities of Samaria.

expand to see more

Hebrew — Kuthah / Kuth, Mesopotamian city.

Policy — Assyrian resettlement of Samaria.

God — Nergal made by the men of Cuth.

Mixture — fear of the LORD with foreign gods.

Warning — emptied land refilled with idols.
